PHYS 1110 Lab 2: Measuring g with a Pendulum

Time ten full swings for each string length, then divide by ten to get the period. Record every value with its unit, and keep the raw times even when a trial looks wrong. The acceleration of gravity follows from the period and the length of the string.

Table 1. Pendulum measurements from the demonstration

Length (m)Ten swings (s)Period (s)g (m/s2)
0.208.980.8989.79
0.4012.691.2699.81
0.6015.551.5559.80
0.8017.941.7949.81

The four values agree to within a quarter of a per cent. Most of the spread comes from the moment the stopwatch is started and stopped, not from the length of the string.

Name: ______________________ Section: ________ Date: ____________

Key terms

PeriodThe time the pendulum takes to swing out and come back to where it started, measured in seconds.
AmplitudeHow far the bob moves away from its resting point; keep it small so the period does not depend on it.
UncertaintyAn estimate of how far the measured value could be from the true one, written with the same unit as the value.
